title: Compact temporal prefix index for cross-request prompt cache reuse
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a compact, temporally-aware prefix index that enables aggressive reuse and deduplication of prefix KV across concurrent and sequential requests while minimizing GPU memory overhead and preserving latency SLOs. Target multiple workloads: short assistant prompts, streaming chat sessions, and batched inference flows.
background: Current prefix/prompt caching stores full prefix KV frames keyed by long fingerprints. This leads to memory duplication when many requests share overlapping prefixes (for example similar system prompts, reused instruction templates, or multi-turn conversations with shared context). The runtime's continuous batching pipeline also increases the lifetime of KV tensors, aggravating GPU memory pressure during bursts. Previous efforts (ENG-25714, ENG-24601) explored canonicalization and sharing; this ticket aims to introduce a compact, temporal index and eviction scheme that deduplicates at the fragment-level and is optimized for GPU pinned memory layout.
goals: 1) Reduce duplicate KV tensor copies in GPU memory by >= 40% on representative webchat workload. 2) Keep median tail latency increase <= 5ms for p95-sensitive routes. 3) Integrate with continuous batching so deduped fragments are fast to attach to a request's KV cache. 4) Provide deterministic eviction and accounting for multi-tenant dedication and isolation policies.
proposed_solution: Create a fragment-oriented prefix registry that stores content-addressed fragments (4KB-64KB grains) in a compact index. Each fragment gets a short 64-bit fingerprint and a reference-counted metadata entry in CPU-side index with an on-GPU allocation pool for hot fragments. Use an LRU+age-window eviction to favor recent fragments (temporal locality) while bounding GPU resident memory. At request time, compute fragment fingerprints from canonicalized prompt segments, look up matches in the registry, and perform a zero-copy attach by mapping the GPU allocation or copying only missing sub-fragments. Integrate with the batching scheduler to coalesce lookups for batch members and pre-pin hot fragments during bursts.
design_decisions:
- Fragment size is adaptive: default 16KB with heuristics to split large prefixes and merge tiny ones.
- Fingerprint: use xxh128 truncated to 64 bits for speed + low collision risk; collisions detected via short content equality checks.
- Index: CPU-resident hash table with memory-mapped metadata and compact bitset for residency.
- GPU residency pool: slab allocator with fixed-size buckets for common fragment sizes; avoids many small cudaMallocs.
- Eviction: hybrid LRU by access recency + temporal window to give priority to fragments accessed within last T seconds (configurable).
- Isolation: tenant-scoped tags so Dedicated customers can opt-out of cross-tenant sharing; default hosted mode allows safe cross-customer fragment sharing for non-sensitive prefixes.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Collision risk: run equality check per collision and escalate fatal collisions to telemetry; extremely unlikely with chosen hash.
- Latency spikes on lookup/mapping: mitigate by batching lookups and prefetching hot fragments.
- Increased CPU memory due to index: keep metadata compact and offload cold entries to disk-backed store if pressure detected.
- Security: ensure fragments from different customers are not shared when tenant isolation flag is set; add audit events when cross-tenant sharing occurs.
implementation_tasks:
1) Design compact index layout + metadata schema and document it in design doc (drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/prefix-fragment-index).
2) Implement fragmenter and canonicalization rules in tokenizer service.
3) Implement CPU-side registry with refcounts and residency bitset.
4) Implement GPU slab allocator and mapping APIs in runtime core.
5) Add batching coalescer hooks to query registry per-batch, avoiding duplicate lookups.
6) Add eviction controller with metrics and runtime config knobs.
7) Add test harness and microbenchmarks (synthetic chat, demo app).
8) Add telemetry: fragment hits, misses, memory saved, lookup latency.
9) Implement rollbacks/fallbacks to existing full-prefix store if registry unavailable.
10) Code review and merge PRs.
PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4312, https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4399
acceptance_criteria:
- Integration tests pass and fallback path exercised.
- Microbenchmarks show >= 40% GPU memory reduction on webchat workload with default config.
- p95 latency for targeted route increases by <= 5ms compared to baseline.
- No cross-tenant sharing when isolation flag enabled (unit/integration tests).
- Telemetry emits fragment hit/miss rates and memory accounting.
- Feature flag gated rollout with config in console and CLI.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for fragmenter, fingerprinting, and equality checks.
- Integration tests for attach/mapping and refcounting under concurrent access.
- Stress test with continuous batching simulator to validate no memory leaks and eviction correctness.
- End-to-end perf tests against internal chat workload and a longer-form prompt generator workload.
- Chaos test: kill registry process mid-batch and ensure graceful fallback.
- Security test for tenant isolation and audit log verification.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Canary run on <5% traffic for non-SLA routes (dev environment). 3) Expand to 25% of routing groups with monitoring. 4) Promote to production for all hosted routes, then Dedicated opt-ins. 5) Expose knob in Console to control temporal window and fragment size.
Rollback: disable feature flag to fall back to full-prefix cache behavior.
monitoring_and_metrics: Metrics to add: fragment_registry_hits_total, fragment_registry_misses_total, gpu_fragment_memory_bytes, average_fragment_lookup_ms, fragment_evictions_total, fragment_collision_detected_total. Dashboards: per-route memory saved and hit-rate heatmap. Alert rules: sustained miss-rate > 70% for 5m, GPU fragment memory > 90% of pool.
notes:
- Prototype early showed 48% memory savings on a 4k token chat simulation but increased CPU lookups by ~8ms; batching coalescing reduced that to ~2ms.
- Need follow-up ticket to support encrypted fragment storage for Private on-prem KMS integration.
- Consider a variant that stores only KV-shared attention heads for some model families to further reduce memory.
